title: Outbox durability outcome vs prescribed mechanism
description:
File: draft-atwood-jmap-chat-federation-00.md
Lines: 594-595

Current text:
  "Outbound messages MUST be queued in a persistent outbox before the first delivery attempt. This ensures that messages are not lost if the remote server is temporarily unreachable or if the local server restarts between the time a message is created and the time delivery is confirmed."

The interop concern is the *durability outcome*: messages survive local restart prior to delivery confirmation. A persistent outbox is one implementation. Others that satisfy the outcome:
- Synchronous write-through to durable backing storage
- Replicated in-memory queues with at-least-once delivery from an upstream broker
- Queueing inside a transactional DB transaction that also performs the local message-store write

Suggested rewording:
  "Outbound messages MUST be durable across local server restart prior to delivery confirmation; the specific mechanism (persistent outbox, write-through queue, transactional store, etc.) is implementation-defined."
acceptance_criteria:
- The MUST clause expresses durability *outcome*, not a specific data-structure mechanism
- Examples of viable implementations listed as non-normative
- No change to the retry/backoff numerics at lines 599-601 (already correctly impl-defined)
